title: DPOY Reese is Too Mean for Anybody on the NY Liberty Bench
meta_description: Three days after winning DPOY, Angel Reese had four steals from four Liberty players in a 92-82 Dream win.
hook: Three days after she was named Defensive Player of the Year, Angel Reese went out and took the ball from four different New York Liberty players in one playoff game. Four steals, three blocks, 17 points, and the Dream won Game 1 92-82. And the play that sealed it wasn't even a bucket of hers. It was the kick-out she threw with 1:30 left.
summary: Atlanta Dream 92, New York Liberty 82, on October 4, 2026, at State Farm Arena. Atlanta leads the best-of-five 1-0. Body is Ryan's bot draft, edited against ESPN game 401918295 and the WNBA.com DPOY release of October 1, 2026. The 3:43 basket is a driving layup plus a missed free throw. Subhead 'Reese the best' is now 'Reese's line'.
hero_image_alt: Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream in a white jersey, number 5, looking up with her mouth open at Target Center
hero_image_credit: Photo: John McClellan / CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons File:Angel Reese Dream (cropped).jpg. Taken May 9, 2026, at Target Center in Minneapolis.
unique: Reese's four steals were Marine Johannes in the second quarter (putback and a made free throw), Breanna Stewart at 6:47, Han Xu at 5:49, and Leonie Fiebich at 4:57
The 3:43 fourth-quarter basket was a driving layup and a missed free throw, leaving the score 82-75
Those third-quarter steals sat inside a 20-2 Atlanta run that turned a 43-39 deficit into a 59-45 lead
The October 1 DPOY release (46 votes, 26 more than Gabby Williams, first Dream winner, 521 rebounds) is set next to this Game 1 line
unverified: The lines that awards fuel her, that the 1:30 kick-out sealed it, that New York has the shooters to bounce back, and that the series will be short are opinion. New York scored after 87-77. The final was 92-82.
The lead photo is from May 9, 2026, at Target Center, not from this game. The caption says so.
The Commons author field says John Mac (Flickr johnmac612). The file description credits John McClellan, and the caption uses that name.

categories.name: Accuracy
categories.reason: Score, quarters, the 20-2 run from 43-39 to 59-45, the 16-point lead cut to 80-75 at 4:00, the 3:43 layup and missed free throw, the 2:24 Canada assist for 84-77, the 1:30 kick-out for 87-77, Reese's line (17 points, 6-of-10, 7 rebounds, 4 offensive, 4 steals, 3 blocks, 2 assists, 34 minutes, plus-7, 4 turnovers, 4-of-6 free throws), the 24-foot three, and New York's 21 turnovers were checked on ESPN game 401918295. The DPOY date (Oct. 1, 2026), 46 votes, Gabby Williams's 20 (26 fewer), 12.1 rebounds a game, 521 rebounds, 206 offensive rebounds, 32 double-doubles, the 500-rebound first, and the first Dream winner match the WNBA.com release. The linked URL is the right release. The photo is a different game, and the caption says so.

categories.name: Originality
categories.reason: The angle is the DPOY announcement three days earlier, then the four steals and the kick-out that made it 87-77. It is not a wire rewrite, and it is still a game story.
